name: Dupilumab
drug_class: Anti-IL-4 receptor α monoclonal antibody (IL-4/IL-13 inhibitor)
route_note: Subcutaneous injection every 2 or 4 weeks (weekly in some indications) by pre-filled pen or syringe

discovery.note: Fully human IgG4 antibody against IL-4Rα, generated with Regeneron's VelocImmune mice; co-developed with Sanofi. Year is the priority date of the Regeneron IL-4R antibody patent (US 7,608,693).

tagline: IL-4/IL-13 blocker treating atopic dermatitis, asthma and other type 2 diseases
summary: Dupilumab is a human monoclonal antibody that blocks the shared IL-4 receptor α subunit, inhibiting signalling by both IL-4 and IL-13. It treats a range of type 2 inflammatory diseases, including atopic dermatitis, asthma, nasal polyps, eosinophilic oesophagitis, prurigo nodularis, chronic urticaria, COPD with eosinophilia and bullous pemphigoid.
mechanism: IL-4 and IL-13 are central type 2 cytokines. IL-4 acts through the type I receptor (IL-4Rα with γc) and both cytokines through the type II receptor (IL-4Rα with IL-13Rα1), activating JAK–STAT6.
Dupilumab binds IL-4Rα and blocks both receptor types, reducing IgE class switching, eosinophil recruitment, mucus production, airway hyperresponsiveness, skin barrier dysfunction and itch.
uses: Moderate to severe atopic dermatitis (from 6 months of age)
Moderate to severe eosinophilic or oral-corticosteroid-dependent asthma

history.title: Collaboration
history.detail: Sanofi and Regeneron's antibody collaboration includes the IL-4Rα programme.

history.title: FDA approval
history.detail: Approved in March for moderate to severe atopic dermatitis; EU approval follows in September.

history.title: Asthma
history.detail: Approved as add-on maintenance for moderate to severe asthma.

history.title: Nasal polyps
history.detail: Approved for chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyps.

history.title: EoE and prurigo nodularis
history.detail: First drug approved in the US for eosinophilic oesophagitis and for prurigo nodularis.

history.title: COPD
history.detail: Approved for COPD with an eosinophilic phenotype in the EU (July) and US (September), the first biologic for COPD.

history.title: Urticaria and pemphigoid
history.detail: FDA approves it for chronic spontaneous urticaria (April) and bullous pemphigoid (June).

pk.half_life: Not well defined (target-mediated); concentrations fall below detection ~10–13 weeks after last dose
pk.metabolism: Proteolytic catabolism to peptides and amino acids (no CYP metabolism)
pk.excretion: Not renally excreted as intact antibody; cleared by catabolism and target-mediated uptake

facts: Conjunctivitis is much more common in atopic dermatitis patients treated with dupilumab than in other indications.
It was the first biologic approved for COPD.
